Text: Fluid and salt imbalance:
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood. Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these and is more likely at higher doses, during rapid fluid loss, if you have severe cirrhosis, or after long-term use.. Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
- dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
- drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
- muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
- fast heartbeat
- passing much less urine than usual
- nausea or vomiting
- seizures
Kidney and liver problems:

The relation 'has increased risk of hypokalemia during' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug is associated with an increased likelihood of developing hypokalemia during periods of rapid fluid loss.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

B. 'has recommended treatment for severe hypoglycemia': The subject drug is associated with the use of the specified medical intervention to manage severe hypoglycemia.
C. 'has test interference effect': The subject drug may cause a false positive or false negative result in the specified diagnostic test.
